opening.text: There was a girl called Lucia Rossi whose family loved picnics in the forest near their home.
For weeks, Lucia helped plan a birthday picnic: sandwiches, juice and a big birthday cake.
On picnic morning, the forecast said showers. "We won't cancel," said Lucia. "We just need a shelter that keeps everything dry!"

guide.brief: I'm PopAI, your story guide. The Rossi family needs a rain shelter that packs into a backpack and goes up in under 5 minutes. Can you help Lucia build it? Let's start!
guide.your_idea: Some engineers already have a spark of an idea for a quick, portable shelter. Do you?
guide.nature_clues: Nature has been shedding rain for millions of years. Tap each card to meet four heroes who stay dry!
guide.design_secret: Here's the secret of the lotus leaf…
guide.skill: Scientists predict before they test. Which surface will make the most drops roll off?
guide.sketch: Time to draw your shelter like a real engineer!
guide.build_and_test:
You started with a first idea. You may have sketched it, built it, or both.
Now you have another possibility—or an improved version of your original idea. You can build and test this version too.
Engineers repeat this cycle: develop an idea, build, test, learn, and improve.
guide.retry_tip: Engineers never stop at round 1. Change the roof angle or the material, and test again!
guide.ending: And ever since then, the Rossi family packs YOUR shelter for every picnic. Rain or shine, the cake stays dry!

quick_check.question: The shelter must go up in under 5 minutes. Lucia's goes up in 3 minutes. How much time is left over?
quick_check.right: Right! 2 whole minutes to spare, so the picnic is covered before the first drop lands!
quick_check.wrong: Not quite. Try 5 minutes take away 3 minutes.

clue_cards.name: Lotus leaf
clue_cards.trick: It is covered in microscopic waxy bumps.
clue_cards.does: Drops sit on the bump tips, roll right off and carry dirt away.

clue_cards.name: Duck
clue_cards.trick: Its feathers overlap like roof tiles and are coated in oil.
clue_cards.does: Rain slides straight off, so the duck stays dry underneath.

clue_cards.name: Rainforest leaf
clue_cards.trick: The leaf ends in a long, pointed drip tip.
clue_cards.does: Rain drains off the point quickly, so the leaf dries fast.

clue_cards.name: Woodpecker
clue_cards.trick: Its nest hole usually faces away from the wind and rain.
clue_cards.does: Rain can't blow or drip inside, so the nest stays dry.

predict.prompt: Soak in or roll off? Predict first!
predict.explain: On the lotus and the feather, water only touches the tips of tiny waxy bumps or an oily coat, so it can't spread out and soak in. Surfaces like this are called superhydrophobic: water-hating!

lab.title: The drip lab
lab.predict: Tilt each surface at the same angle and add 10 drops. Which one will make the most drops roll off?

tool.name: Mind map
tool.intro: A mind map is a drawing of your thinking. One big idea goes in the middle, and smaller ideas grow out from it like a tree. Today you'll learn the first 3 pieces.

parts.name: Centre
parts.what: Write the big question in the middle.
parts.example: 🚲 Write "a better bike" in the middle of the page.
parts.starter: In the centre of my map I'll write…

parts.name: Branches
parts.what: Draw lines out to the main topics.
parts.example: 🚲 Branches for wheels, seat and brakes.
parts.starter: My branches for staying dry are shape, surface and…

parts.name: Twigs
parts.what: Add smaller ideas to each branch.
parts.example: 🚲 On the wheels branch: tyres, spokes, a pump.
parts.starter: On the surface branch I'll add the lotus leaf and…

partner_lessons.secret: Rain drops land on a lotus leaf, roll straight off, and even carry dirt away with them.
partner_lessons.how: The leaf is covered in microscopic bumps topped with wax. A drop only touches the tips of the bumps, so it cannot spread out and soak in. It stays round and rolls away. Scientists call this the lotus effect.
inspiration: What if Lucia’s shelter had a roof with a bumpy, waxy surface, so the rain beads up and rolls away like on a lotus leaf?
partner_lessons.your_turn: How could you give your shelter’s roof a “lotus” surface? What would you use, and where would the rain go?

hint.text: Look closely at the lotus leaf’s surface. Tiny waxy bumps keep each drop from touching most of the leaf, so the drop stays round and rolls away.
hint.ask: What could you create with a surface that makes water bead up and roll away in a similar way?

partner_lessons.secret: A duck can swim in the rain all day and its body underneath stays dry.
partner_lessons.how: Its feathers overlap like roof tiles, and the duck spreads oil on them from a gland near its tail. The overlap sends water down and away, and the oil helps water slide off instead of soaking in.
inspiration: What if Lucia’s shelter were made of overlapping pieces, like duck feathers or roof tiles, so water always runs down and off?
partner_lessons.your_turn: Which pieces could you overlap for your shelter, and which way would they face so the water runs off?

hint.text: Look at how a duck’s feathers lie. They overlap like tiles, all pointing the same way, and their oil helps water slide off.
hint.ask: What could you create from overlapping pieces that send water down and away in a similar way?

partner_lessons.secret: Leaves in the rainforest dry quickly, even though it rains there almost every day.
partner_lessons.how: Many of them end in a long, pointed “drip tip”. Water runs along the leaf to the tip and drips off from one spot, so less water stays on the leaf.
inspiration: What if Lucia’s shelter had drip tips at its edges, so the rain drips off away from the picnic?
partner_lessons.your_turn: Where would you put drip tips on your shelter, and where would you want the water to land?

hint.text: Look at the tip of the rainforest leaf. Water runs to the pointed tip and drips off from one spot.
hint.ask: What could you create that guides the water to drip off where you want it to?

partner_lessons.secret: A woodpecker’s nest hole stays dry inside, even in a storm.
partner_lessons.how: The hole is usually made facing away from the wind and the rain, so the rain can’t blow or drip in. Its direction protects it.
inspiration: What if Lucia set up the shelter with its open side facing away from the wind, like a woodpecker’s nest hole?
partner_lessons.your_turn: Which way would your shelter face, and how would you know where the wind and rain come from?

hint.text: Look at which way the woodpecker’s nest hole faces. It points away from the wind and the rain.
hint.ask: How could the direction of your shelter help keep the rain out?
